question: Under Kentucky law, when a principal broker identifies different licensees within the same firm to separately represent more than one party in the same real estate transaction, this arrangement is known as:
choice_a: Designated agency
choice_b: Sub-agency
choice_c: Transaction brokerage
choice_d: Single agency
explanation: KRS 324.010(14) defines "designated agency" as a form of agency relationship that exists when a principal broker, in accordance with KRS 324.121, identifies different licensees in the same firm to separately represent more than one party in the same transaction.

question: Before a principal broker may designate an affiliated licensee to act as the exclusive agent for a seller, buyer, lessor, or lessee to the exclusion of other affiliated licensees, KRS 324.121 requires that the designation procedure be:
choice_a: Approved in advance by the Kentucky Real Estate Commission
choice_b: Made in writing and communicated to all licensees affiliated with the principal broker
choice_c: Filed with the county clerk where the brokerage is located
choice_d: Renewed annually along with the firm's license
explanation: KRS 324.121(1) requires that the designation procedure be made in writing and communicated to all licensees affiliated with the principal broker.

question: A principal broker wants to designate Licensee Ray as the exclusive agent for a seller in an upcoming listing. Under KRS 324.121, whose consent to that designation must be obtained?
choice_a: Only the seller's consent
choice_b: Only the buyer's consent, since the buyer is the party at risk
choice_c: Both the seller's (or lessor's) consent and, where applicable, the buyer's (or lessee's) consent to a corresponding designation
choice_d: No consent is required as long as the designation is in writing
explanation: KRS 324.121(1) requires the designated agent to inform and obtain the consent of the buyer or lessee (or prospective buyer or lessee) to the designation, and separately to inform and obtain the consent of the seller or lessor to the designation.

question: Can a principal broker designate himself or herself as a designated agent under KRS 324.121?
choice_a: Yes, at any time and without restriction
choice_b: Yes, but only with written consent of the Kentucky Real Estate Commission
choice_c: Yes, but only in transactions involving commercial property
choice_d: No, the statute expressly prohibits a principal broker from designating himself or herself as a designated agent
explanation: KRS 324.121(1) states plainly: "The principal broker shall not designate himself or herself as a designated agent."

question: In a Kentucky transaction where a principal broker has designated one licensee to represent the seller and another affiliated licensee to represent the buyer, who is deemed to be the dual agent representing both parties in a limited fiduciary capacity?
choice_a: Only the principal broker or a designated manager working under the principal broker's direction
choice_b: Both designated licensees jointly
choice_c: Neither licensee nor the principal broker — no one is considered a dual agent in this scenario
choice_d: The licensee who first obtained the listing
explanation: KRS 324.121(2) provides that when a principal broker designates separate licensees for the seller and buyer in the same transaction, only the principal broker or a designated manager working under the principal broker's direction is deemed to be the dual agent, representing both in a limited fiduciary capacity.

question: How must a principal broker acting as a dual agent under KRS 324.121 handle confidential information relating to the seller and the buyer?
choice_a: It may be shared freely between the designated agents representing each party
choice_b: It must be kept in an individual file for each party that is maintained and accessed only by the principal broker or designated manager
choice_c: It must be disclosed to both parties simultaneously to ensure fairness
choice_d: It must be forwarded to the Kentucky Real Estate Commission for safekeeping
explanation: KRS 324.121(2) requires the dual agent (principal broker or designated manager) to keep confidential information relating to either party in an individual file maintained and accessed by the principal broker or designated manager only.

question: Under KRS 324.121(2), a principal broker or designated manager acting as a dual agent is prohibited from:
choice_a: Collecting a commission from both parties
choice_b: Supervising the designated agents involved in the transaction
choice_c: Disclosing to either party confidential information learned relative to the other party
choice_d: Communicating with either party without the other's presence
explanation: KRS 324.121(2) states that as a dual agent, the principal broker or designated manager "shall not disclose to either party confidential information learned relative to the other party."

question: In a cooperative sale involving consumers separately represented by nonaffiliated principal brokers or designated managers, KRS 324.121(2) provides that a designated agency arrangement within one firm:
choice_a: Automatically extends dual agency status to the cooperating, unaffiliated broker as well
choice_b: Voids the cooperating broker's agency relationship with their own client
choice_c: Requires the cooperating broker to also designate a dual agent
choice_d: Does not affect the agency relationships in that cooperative sale, except as otherwise set forth in the statute
explanation: KRS 324.121(2) states that, except as set forth in subsection (3), the designation "shall not affect the principal broker's or designated manager's agency relationships in cooperative sales between consumers separately represented by nonaffiliated principal brokers or designated managers."

question: Under KRS 324.121(3), if a seller and a buyer in a Kentucky transaction each happen to know the same fact about the property independently, is that knowledge automatically imputed between the principal broker, designated manager, the firm, and the licensees involved?
choice_a: No — no exchange of information or knowledge between or among consumers, the principal broker, the designated manager, the firm, or the licensees shall be imputed as a matter of law
choice_b: Yes, knowledge held by any consumer is imputed as a matter of law to the brokerage
choice_c: Only if the knowledge relates to a material physical defect
choice_d: Only if both parties are represented by the same designated agent
explanation: KRS 324.121(3) provides that no exchange of information or knowledge between or among consumers (seller, buyer, lessor, or lessee) and the principal broker, designated manager, firm, or licensees shall be imputed as a matter of law in any real estate transaction.

question: Does Kentucky law prohibit real estate brokerage firms and licensees from entering into dual agency relationships with consumers?
choice_a: Yes, dual agency is completely banned in Kentucky
choice_b: No — KRS 324.121(4) states that nothing in the section shall prevent a firm or licensee from entering into a dual agency relationship with consumers in a real estate transaction
choice_c: Dual agency is allowed only in commercial transactions
choice_d: Dual agency requires a special commission-issued permit
explanation: KRS 324.121(4) expressly states that nothing in the section prevents a real estate brokerage firm or licensee from entering into a dual agency relationship with consumers in a real estate transaction, subject to the section's other requirements.

question: Under KRS 324.162 (Agent's duty to disclose), a real estate agent representing a party in the sale, leasing, or exchange of real property has:
choice_a: An unlimited affirmative duty to disclose every fact known about the property to all parties
choice_b: A duty to disclose only if specifically asked by the buyer
choice_c: No affirmative duty to disclose to a person acquiring an interest in the property any information that is not required by KRS Chapter 324 or applicable federal law
choice_d: A duty to disclose limited exclusively to structural defects
explanation: KRS 324.162 provides that a licensed agent representing a party has no affirmative duty to disclose to any person acquiring an interest in real property information not required by KRS Chapter 324 or applicable federal law.

question: KRS 324.360's seller's disclosure of conditions requirement applies to which type of transaction?
choice_a: Any sale of commercial real estate over $1 million
choice_b: Only transactions financed with a conventional mortgage
choice_c: Any lease of residential property regardless of licensee involvement
choice_d: Sales and purchases of single-family residential real estate dwellings where a person licensed under KRS Chapter 324 receives compensation
explanation: KRS 324.360(1) states the section applies to sales and purchases involving single-family residential real estate dwellings if any person licensed under the chapter receives compensation.

question: Who is responsible for promulgating the actual "seller's disclosure of conditions form" used under KRS 324.360?
choice_a: The Kentucky Real Estate Commission, by administrative regulation
choice_b: Each individual principal broker, for their own firm
choice_c: The county property valuation administrator
choice_d: The National Association of Realtors
explanation: KRS 324.360(2) states that the commission shall promulgate an administrative regulation authorizing a "seller's disclosure of conditions form."

question: Which of the following is NOT among the categories of conditions that KRS 324.360(3) specifies must be addressed on the seller's disclosure of conditions form?
choice_a: Basement condition and whether it leaks
choice_b: The property's current appraised market value
choice_c: Source and condition of water supply
choice_d: Source and condition of sewage service
explanation: KRS 324.360(3) lists basement condition/leaks, roof condition/leaks, source and condition of water supply, source and condition of sewage service, working condition of component systems, and other matters the commission deems appropriate. Appraised market value is not one of the listed categories.

question: Under KRS 324.360(4), when must a seller who has listed the property complete and sign the seller's disclosure of conditions form?
choice_a: Within 30 days after closing
choice_b: Only if the buyer specifically requests it
choice_c: At the time the seller executes the listing agreement or similar agreement by which a licensee intends to market the property
choice_d: At the final walkthrough
explanation: KRS 324.360(4) requires the seller to complete and sign the form at the time he or she executes any listing agreement or similar marketing agreement.

question: A Kentucky listing agent receives a written and signed offer to purchase from a prospective buyer. Under KRS 324.360(4), within what time frame must the listing agent deliver a copy of the completed seller's disclosure of conditions form to that prospective purchaser or their representative?
choice_a: Within 24 hours
choice_b: Within 10 business days
choice_c: There is no deadline as long as it is delivered before closing
choice_d: Within 72 hours of the listing agent's receipt of the written and signed offer
explanation: KRS 324.360(4) requires the listing agent to deliver a copy of the form to any prospective purchaser or representative within seventy-two (72) hours of the listing agent's receipt of a written and signed offer to purchase.

question: A Kentucky property is being sold by the owner "for sale by owner" (FSBO) without a listing agreement, but a licensee is involved in presenting an offer. Under KRS 324.360(5), if the owner completes and signs the disclosure form, by when must the licensee deliver it to the buyer or potential buyer?
choice_a: Not later than 120 hours after the creation of any executory contract for sale of the property
choice_b: Not later than 72 hours after the offer is signed
choice_c: At closing only
choice_d: Within 30 days of the owner signing the form
explanation: KRS 324.360(5) requires that in a FSBO transaction where the owner completes and signs the form, the licensee shall deliver the form to the buyer or potential buyer not later than one hundred twenty (120) hours after the creation of any executory contract for sale of the property.

question: Under KRS 324.360(6), who is responsible for retaining the original of the seller's disclosure of conditions form?
choice_a: The buyer's agent
choice_b: The listing broker, or the broker of any licensee who presents an offer on a property not subject to a listing agreement
choice_c: The Kentucky Real Estate Commission
choice_d: The title company handling closing
explanation: KRS 324.360(6) states the original of the form shall be retained by the listing broker or by the broker of any licensee who presents an offer on a property not subject to a listing agreement.

question: Under KRS 324.360(7), the seller's disclosure of conditions form is NOT required for which of the following?
choice_a: A resale of an existing single-family home listed with a broker
choice_b: Any transaction involving a first-time homebuyer
choice_c: A residential purchase of a new home if a warranty is offered, a sale of real estate at auction, or a court-supervised foreclosure
choice_d: Any transaction under $150,000
explanation: KRS 324.360(7) exempts the form requirement for residential purchases of new homes if a warranty is offered, sales of real estate at auction, and court-supervised foreclosures.

question: If a Kentucky seller refuses to complete and sign the disclosure of conditions form, what does KRS 324.360(8) require?
choice_a: The transaction must be cancelled immediately
choice_b: The Kentucky Real Estate Commission must be notified within 24 hours
choice_c: The listing agent must complete the form on the seller's behalf instead
choice_d: The refusal must be communicated in writing by the broker or sales associate involved in the transaction to the purchaser or prospective purchaser, without unreasonable delay
explanation: KRS 324.360(8) requires that if the seller refuses to complete and sign the form, the refusal be communicated in writing by the broker or sales associate involved in the transaction to the purchaser or prospective purchaser without unreasonable delay.

question: Under KRS 324.360(9), when may a real estate licensee complete a portion of the seller's disclosure of conditions form?
choice_a: Only if the licensee is the owner of the property, or has been requested by the owner to do so, with that request acknowledged in writing on the form
choice_b: At any time, since the licensee has superior knowledge of the property
choice_c: Only after obtaining approval from the Kentucky Real Estate Commission
choice_d: Never — a licensee is absolutely barred from touching the form under any circumstances
explanation: KRS 324.360(9) makes it a violation for a licensee to complete any portion of the form unless the licensee is the property owner or has been requested by the owner to complete it, with that request acknowledged in writing on the form; the licensee is then held harmless for representations appearing on the form.

question: Under KRS 324.165, a real estate licensee who has learned that a competing licensee's client has an existing buyer agency agreement:
choice_a: May freely counsel that client on how to terminate or amend the existing agency agreement
choice_b: Is prohibited from counseling that client regarding the manner in which the client may terminate or amend the existing listing contract, buyer agency agreement, or other agency relationship
choice_c: Must report the existing agreement to the Kentucky Real Estate Commission
choice_d: May only discuss termination if the client initiates the conversation in writing
explanation: KRS 324.165(2) prohibits a real estate licensee (or firm, or anyone acting on their behalf) from counseling a client of another licensee regarding how to terminate or amend an existing listing contract, buyer agency agreement, or other agency relationship.
